terra.problem: The punchline treats Jesus’ prayer and the revelation of His glory as a prayer meeting nobody could top. Humor should not target Jesus or a holy moment.
The statement that fasting appears in the Bible is a fact from outside this passage and needs a reference.
The passage does not explicitly say that Jesus was praying while the others were asleep.
Identifying Moses as Israel’s leader and Elijah as a prophet uses facts from outside this passage without references.
Moses’ leadership and his receiving the law at Sinai are facts from outside this passage and need references.
Elijah’s role as a prophet and his connection to Mount Carmel are facts from outside this passage and need references.
The statement that altars appear throughout the Bible is a Bible fact from outside this passage and needs a reference.
The punchline makes the recording of Peter’s words in Scripture part of the joke. The way Scripture is written is not a joke.
The passage does not say Peter came up with the idea on the spot.
The explanation repeats who was present without adding much personality or insight, making it feel flat.
Identifying Moses as Israel’s leader is a fact from outside this passage and needs a reference.
The explanation repeats that Moses was no longer there in several ways and feels flat.
Identifying Elijah as a prophet is a fact from outside this passage and needs a reference.
The passage says Jesus’ face changed and His clothes became radiantly white; it does not say Jesus Himself was glowing.
